lines.rookie: "Koreya! Ura!" means "Korea, hurrah!" He called out for Korea!
lines.junior: "Koreya! Ura!" means "Korea, hurrah!" He was calling out for Korea!
lines.master: "Koreya! Ura!" means "Korea, hurrah!" It was Korea he called out for!

lines.rookie: Rossiya is on the card, but he did not call it out.
lines.junior: Rossiya is on the card, but he did not call that word out.
lines.master: Rossiya is on the card, yet it is not a word he called out.

lines.rookie: Dengi means money. He did not say it.
lines.junior: Dengi means money, but he never said it.
lines.master: Dengi means money, a word he never spoke.

lines.rookie: Ura means hurrah. That is not a country.
lines.junior: Ura means hurrah, but that is not a country.
lines.master: Ura means hurrah, which is no country.

lines.rookie: That is the word he called out. Type it in English.
lines.junior: That is the word he called out. Now type it in English.
lines.master: That is the word as he called it out. Give it in English.

lines.rookie: Harbin is the place, not his country.
lines.junior: Harbin is where it happened, not his country.
lines.master: Harbin is only the place, not his country.

lines.rookie: Mr. Pak heard him call out, "Koreya! Ura!": Korea, hurrah! Not for money: for his country.
lines.junior: Mr. Pak heard him call out, "Koreya! Ura!": Korea, hurrah! It was not for money, but for his country.
lines.master: Mr. Pak heard him call out, "Koreya! Ura!": Korea, hurrah! For his country, not for money.

lines.rookie: Paper A's story came from tea-room talk. The man on the platform heard "Koreya! Ura!"
lines.junior: Paper A's story came from talk in the tea room. The man on the platform heard "Koreya! Ura!"
lines.master: Paper A's story sprang from tea-room talk; the man on the platform heard "Koreya! Ura!"

lines.rookie: The Evening Sheet says:
lines.junior: The Evening Sheet claims:
lines.master: The Evening Sheet asserts:

lines.rookie:
Our writer knows what happened.
He called out nothing.
He wanted money.
lines.junior:
Our writer knows exactly what happened.
He called out nothing.
He wanted money.
lines.master:
Our writer knows precisely what took place.
He called out nothing.
He wanted money.

lines.rookie: Each question needs one card: the times, the words, or Itō.
lines.junior: Each question needs one card: the times, the words, or what Itō did.
lines.master: Every question is answered by one card: the times, the words, or Itō's deeds.

lines.rookie: Where: Mr. Pak's Day. What: Mr. Pak's Words. Why: Mrs. Kang's Note.
lines.junior: Where: Mr. Pak's Day. What: Mr. Pak's Words. Why: Mrs. Kang's Note.
lines.master: Where: Mr. Pak's Day. What: Mr. Pak's Words. Why: Mrs. Kang's Note.

lines.rookie: Mr. Sorin says: "My writer saw it all."
lines.junior: Mr. Sorin says: "My writer saw it all with his own eyes."
lines.master: Mr. Sorin insists: "My writer saw it all, from start to finish."

lines.rookie: Which card has the times of that day?
lines.junior: Which card shows the times of that day?
lines.master: Which card holds the times of that day?

lines.rookie: He called out at 9:30. Your writer came at noon. He did not see it.
lines.junior: He called out at 9:30, but your writer came at noon. He did not see it.
lines.master: He called out at 9:30; your writer only arrived at noon. He saw none of it.

lines.rookie: True. He wrote what the traveller said.
lines.junior: That is true. He wrote down what the traveller told him.
lines.master: True enough. He wrote only what the traveller said.

lines.rookie: Which card has the words Mr. Pak heard?
lines.junior: Which card has the words that Mr. Pak heard?
lines.master: Which card records the words Mr. Pak heard?

lines.rookie: "Koreya! Ura!" It means "Korea, hurrah!" Mr. Pak heard it.
lines.junior: "Koreya! Ura!" It means "Korea, hurrah!", and Mr. Pak heard it.
lines.master: "Koreya! Ura!", that is, "Korea, hurrah!" Mr. Pak heard it himself.

lines.rookie: Mr. Sorin asks: "Why would a man do this for Korea? What had Itō done to Korea?"
lines.junior: Mr. Sorin asks: "Why would a man do this for Korea? What had Itō done to it?"
lines.master: Mr. Sorin asks: "Why would a man do this for Korea? What had Itō done to that country?"

lines.rookie: That does not tell me what Itō did.
lines.junior: That doesn't tell me what Itō did.
lines.master: That says nothing of what Itō did.

lines.rookie: Which card talks about Itō and 1905?
lines.junior: Which card tells about Itō and 1905?
lines.master: Which card speaks of Itō and 1905?

lines.rookie: Itō forced the 1905 treaty on Korea. Korea lost the right to deal with other countries.
lines.junior: Itō forced the 1905 treaty on Korea, so Korea lost the right to deal with other countries.
lines.master: Itō forced the 1905 treaty on Korea, and with it Korea lost the right to deal with other countries.

lines.rookie: So he did it for his country, not for money. I will print that.
lines.junior: So he did it for his country, not for money. I will print that.
lines.master: Then he acted for his country, not for money. I will print that.
